extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent examiners, IP policymakers, and industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO press release summarizing an Office of the Chief Economist report measuring patent examination outcomes (first-action rejections and uncertainty) for technologies affected by the Supreme Court's Alice decision, especially before and after the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent subject matter eligibility (Section 101) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of whether claimed inventions satisfy Section 101 subject matter eligibility; the page attributes improved analysis to the USPTO's January 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2019 PEG is presented as the framework that 'greatly improved the analysis' of Section 101 determinations across technologies affected by Alice. Use the 2019 PEG's approach when assessing eligibility (as reflected in the USPTO's conclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of receiving a first office action rejection for patent-ineligible subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A measurable examination outcome: the probability that an application in Alice-affected technologies receives a first office action rejecting claims as patent-ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report finds this likelihood 'decreased by 25%' one year after the 2019 PEG compared to the prior year; this metric is used to evaluate the practical impact of guidance changes on examination behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty about determinations of patent subject matter eligibility in the first action stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A measured level of uncertainty or variability in first-action Section 101 determinations for affected technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report measures this uncertainty and reports it 'decreased by 44%' over the first year following publication of the 2019 PEG compared to the previous year; lower uncertainty is treated as a positive outcome (more predictability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability and certainty of eligibility determinations in Alice-affected technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which examiners' and applicants' expectations about subject matter eligibility are stable and predictable in technology areas most affected by the Alice decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release highlights that USPTO actions 'have brought greater predictability and certainty' to eligibility determinations; predictability is framed as beneficial to innovators and investors and as a policy goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: First office action stage as a key evaluation point
rubrics_metrics.description: The first-office-action stage of examination is identified as the focal stage for measuring both rejection likelihood and uncertainty regarding Section 101 determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics reported (25% reduction in rejection likelihood; 44% reduction in uncertainty) specifically reference the first action stage, implying that early-stage examination outcomes are a primary indicator of guidance effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG) as an intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2019 PEG is treated as the policy intervention whose issuance the report evaluates for effects on examination outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release attributes measured improvements (reduced rejection rates and uncertainty) to the issuance and use of the 2019 PEG and promotes its role in stabilizing subject matter eligibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based evaluation of policy impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The report is described as using empirical, evidence-based methods to assess how the Alice decision and USPTO guidance affected examination outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief Economist frames the analysis as 'evidence-based' and uses quantitative outcome measures (rejection likelihood, uncertainty) to judge the guidance's impact; this implies a standard of using empirical metrics to evaluate policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary economic function of the patent system: incentivize innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: A normative criterion: the patent system's primary economic function is to provide incentives for greater innovation, entrepreneurship, and job creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release cites this norm to justify why predictability and proper application of subject matter eligibility rules matter for policy — evaluations of guidance are therefore tied to how they support innovation and investment.
